title: More ways to make and remake images
summary:
Image-making gained new models and community tools, while Enter’s request paths and tier information got less mysterious.

Seedream 4.0 joined the Nectar image models, then gained support for images up to 4096×4096 pixels, with a 1024×1024 default when dimensions are omitted. Nanobanana was added for image-to-image generation through Enter. Community projects explored the other end of the workflow: Opposite Prompt Generator turns an idea into its semantic opposite, while ReImagine transforms or combines images on mobile.

Enter’s image proxy received fixes for forwarding request details and resolving kontext correctly. Enter requests now bypass the IP queue, and Enter nanobanana requests skip its hourly per-IP check; other nanobanana requests remain limited to 10 images per hour. Flux errors now return the original failure instead of silently switching models. Debugging an image request should involve fewer surprises, a modest ambition for software.

A GET text-generation endpoint now accepts a prompt in the URL and an optional model. Enter added copyable publishable API keys that work in the `key` query parameter for GET text and image URLs; secret keys still use the Authorization header. Generation routes also accept a session cookie or Bearer API key, and chat completions handle omitted models or empty message arrays.

The tier panel grew from assigned-tier and checkout information into a clearer view of subscription status, product name, daily Pollen and refill timing. It now reads product details from Polar rather than hardcoded values, alongside updated Seed, Flower and Nectar product detection. Enter also removed an inaccurate countdown and disabled top-up buttons that led to checkout.
